name: Launch
text: This is MatchOS. Three perspectives. Let's run the actual press-resistance demo.

name: Independent choices
text: Judge demo replays one match state. Each persona independently chooses a story. Here, the broadcaster highlights Liverpool playing through City's press.

name: Four languages
text: The fan gets Liverpool's story in Spanish. Viewers choose English, French, Spanish or Hindi.

name: Voice and analysis
text: Microsoft Voice speaks their language. The analyst focuses on tactical detail.

name: Evidence
text: Inspect the editorial decision and supporting facts. Then open the source events on the pitch. Every story stays connected to its evidence.

name: Broadcast
text: Broadcast reuses stories that already aired. Choose an audience to preview on-screen graphics, open a separate graphics window, or see their match-so-far recap. The same published story drives each view.

name: Evaluations
text: Evaluations shows saved tests, not live match updates. The dropdown chooses a test run. Each row tests one audience in one situation. Passed means the expected checks succeeded. Holding a repeated story can be correct.

name: How it works
text: Agent Framework shares evidence across independent audience workflows. Decision One chooses; GPT six Luna writes. Telemetry records each step. Azure Container Apps hosts the app.

name: Partnership opportunity
text: MatchOS could extend Microsoft's Premier League partnership: personal app stories, broadcast graphics, and multilingual catch-up, built on licensed live feeds. This demo uses synthetic data. One match. Every perspective.
